title: U.S. House · Texas's 17th District
area: Central Texas, including parts of Waco and the Bryan-College Station area.

context.text: Incumbent Pete Sessions (R) ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Casey Shepard won the Democratic nomination in a May 26, 2026 primary runoff over Jamilah Flores, who had unofficially withdrawn but remained on the runoff ballot.

candidates.name: Pete Sessions

summary.text: Pete Sessions is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Texas's 17th District. A Waco native who spent 16 years at Southwestern Bell Telephone Company, he was first elected to Congress in 1996, chaired the House Rules Committee from 2013 to 2019, and returned to the House in 2021 after losing in 2018. He chairs the Government Operations Subcommittee of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.

background.text: Born in Waco, Texas, in 1955. He attended local public schools through ninth grade, then Winston Churchill High School in San Antonio.
Earned a B.S. from Southwestern University in 1978, and later spent twelve years on the university's Board of Trustees.
Worked 16 years for Southwestern Bell Telephone Company, retiring as District Manager, according to his official biography. (Ballotpedia describes his career as working as an executive with AT&T.)
His father, William Sessions, was a federal district judge and the fourth Director of the FBI, appointed by President Ronald Reagan.
First elected to Congress in 1996. His official biography says he spent a decade in House Republican leadership and chaired the National Republican Congressional Committee from 2009 through 2012.
Chaired the House Committee on Rules from 2013 to 2019.

Lost the November 2018 general election in Texas's 32nd District to Democrat Colin Allred, then won the Republican nomination and the November 3, 2020 general election in the 17th District, defeating Democrat Rick Kennedy and Libertarian Ted Brown.

His official biography credits him with sponsoring the Family Opportunity Act of 2005 (enacted 2006) and the Border Tunnel Task Force Act (passed 2018). In the 119th Congress he chairs the Government Operations Subcommittee of the Oversight and Government Reform Committee and sits on the Financial Services Committee.

According to his official biography, he, his father, and two sons are Eagle Scouts, and he has held leadership roles with the Boy Scouts of America; he lives in Waco with his wife, Karen, and they have five sons.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, chairing its Government Operations Subcommittee, and on the Health Care and Financial Services Subcommittee and the Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Casey Shepard
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff over Jamilah Flores.

summary.text: Casey Shepard is the Democratic nominee challenging Sessions. A seventh-generation Texan and attorney, she describes graduating from Loyola Marymount University on a debate scholarship and earning a law degree from UC Davis. She is campaigning on food and housing assistance, health-care access, and government accountability.

background.text: Describes herself as a seventh-generation Texan and a third-generation Central Texan, and graduated from Midway High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Loyola Marymount University in 2003, where she says she went on a debate scholarship after discovering a passion for public policy debate in high school.
Earned a law degree from the University of California, Davis School of Law (Martin Luther King Jr. Hall) in 2007; Ballotpedia lists her profession as attorney.
Placed second in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary (32.4%) and won the May 26, 2026 runoff over Jamilah Flores, who had withdrawn but remained on the ballot, 59.9% to 40.1%.

priorities.text: Legislative priorities of food stability, healthcare access, and affordable housing, including strengthening SNAP, WIC, school meals, and ACA premium subsidies.
priorities.quote: During the fight on Capitol Hill, my legislative priorities are food stability, healthcare access, and affordable housing.

priorities.text: Focuses on scrutinizing executive agencies and holding officials accountable for respecting the limits of their authority.
priorities.quote: My focus will be accountability. That means working with others to scrutinize executive agencies, investigate misconduct, and act when institutions fail the people they're meant to serve.

priorities.text: Wants to expand mental-health programs, citing the economic and social costs of untreated illness.

positions.summary: Wants to improve ACA premium subsidies, Medicaid, CHIP, and SAMHSA mental-health programs.
His campaign website calls for ending tariffs that raise food prices and construction material costs.
positions.quote: Rebuild global food stability by restoring the USAID Food Program and ending tariffs that raise food prices.

positions.summary: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he lists a renewable-energy economy and climate change action among the priorities he would work on with Democratic coalitions.
positions.quote: a renewable‑energy economy, climate change action

candidates.researchNotes: Shepard's biography comes from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website or employment details beyond 'attorney' were located.
